summary: Oxford County, ME: fire tower on Speckled Mountain built 1914, moved to Streaked Mountain in 1987; only foundations remain at the summit in the White Mountain National Forest.

facts.status_note: Tower moved to Streaked Mountain in 1987; only the foundations remain at the summit per Section Hiker

staffing.status: fire watchmen reached the tower by a jeep track until the track was closed in the 1970s; no watchman named in the sources read

access.note: Summit lies in the Caribou-Speckled Wilderness of the White Mountain National Forest and is reached on foot by hiking trails

visit.trail_note: State hike guide describes Bickford Brook and Blueberry Ridge Trails as an 8.2-mile loop; Section Hiker describes the Cold Brook Trail route. No tower stands at the summit to climb.

events.note: Tower listed at Speckled Mountain, Stoneham, first dated 1914

notes_for_editor: The 1914 build date rests on one newspaper roundup. A Facebook group post seen only in a search snippet says a tower was built in 1919 by the National Forest Service; not used because it is unverified social media. Staffing evidence is thin: watchmen used the jeep track, but no names or dates were found. Streaked Mountain's 1987 replacement appears in both the Sun Journal and the hike guide, consistent with the move. The hike guide misspells the name as Specked in one line; the quote is kept as printed. Status is recorded as gone (tower), with the foundations in the status note; change to ruins if preferred.
